subject: URGENT: short-notice runtime safeguard deployment and customer guidance
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: DataWave Ops <ops@datawave.ai>, Nancy Ruiz <nancy@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: URGENT: short-notice runtime safeguard deployment and customer guidance

Team —

We’re initiating a short-notice safeguard deploy to mitigate an observed memory-growth regression in our scheduler on certain GPU configurations (A100 40GB with 4-shard packing). The issue can cause degraded KV cache eviction leading to elevated tail latency for long-history chat sessions.

What we are doing now:
- Rolling a minimal safeguard at 09:30 UTC that reduces max-batch-size and disables cross-shard prefix compaction for affected hosts. This is a behavioral change only (no model weights altered).
- Routing affected customers to a fallback shard pool for 15–45 minutes during the rollout to avoid throttling.

Customer action requested (DataWave / Orbit):
- No immediate action required. We recommend pinning long-running chat routes to smaller context lengths (<= 4k tokens) if you can — see runbook link below.
- If you see sustained errors > 5% or token-level throttles, reply to this thread with logs and we’ll prioritize a rollback.

Impact window: 09:30 — 10:15 UTC (expected), may be extended if we detect regression after rollout.

Attachments: safeguard_v1.patch (patch/minified), runbook-incident-20280914.pdf (pdf)

We’ll post updates here every 15 minutes or sooner if anything materially changes. Apologies for the short notice — this is an operational safeguard to avoid wider customer impact.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai
From: DataWave Ops <ops@datawave.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 09:25:30 -0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: short-notice runtime safeguard deployment and customer guidance

Thanks Logan — we saw the advisory.

A couple quick questions:
1) If you do the safeguard rollout and we observe a spike, is there a hard rollback plan we can trigger from our side (API toggle or a contact to flip)?
2) Is there any expected change in cost or request latency once the safeguard is active?

We’re monitoring our end and can provide traces if you want them.

— Clara (on behalf of DataWave)
Clara Montes, Platform Ops
ops@datawave.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 09:34:10 -0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: short-notice runtime safeguard deployment and customer guidance

Flagging the rollout checklist and rollback triggers — internal only:

1) Pre-rollout (09:28 UTC) — snapshot telemetry, mark canary hosts (hosts-az-west-2-{12..15})
2) Deploy safeguard_v1.patch to canary (09:30 UTC) — this toggles two knobs: batch_limit=32 -> 16, enable_cross_shard_compaction=false
3) Monitor latency, error-rate, and KV miss-rate on canary for 5m.
4) If error-rate > 2.5% OR tail latency (p99.9) increases > 80ms -> immediate rollback and migrate affected customers to fallback pool.

Rollback procedure (manual):
- runbook command: /rollout rollback INC-2028-0914-01 --canary-hosts hosts-az-west-2-12..15
- if customer requests rollback, we’ll execute and confirm in-thread within 10 minutes.

Notes: this is a low-risk behavioral change; we’ve prepared a fast revert. Attached runbook has play-by-play commands.

Attachments: runbook-incident-20280914.pdf (pdf)

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: DataWave Ops <ops@datawave.ai>, Nancy Ruiz <nancy@orbit-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Sep 2028 12:03:00 -0000
Subject: RE: URGENT: short-notice runtime safeguard deployment and customer guidance

Update for DataWave / Orbit / partners —

Summary: safeguard_v1 rolled to canary at 09:30 UTC, promoted gradually to affected hosts by 09:52 UTC. We observed a small, transient increase in request latency for ~3 minutes on the initial canary (p95 + ~30ms) and no persistent error-rate increase. Rollback was NOT required.

What we changed for affected hosts: reduced max batch size and disabled cross-shard prefix compaction to prevent unbounded KV cache pressure. This will slightly increase per-token compute on the affected hosts (estimated +2–5% cost) while the behavioral safeguard is active. We’ll revert the knobs as soon as a targeted fix for the scheduler compaction algorithm is validated (ETA next 72 hours).

Customer guidance:
- No action required. If you rely on very long contexts (>40k tokens) we recommend reducing context or routing those sessions to a dedicated pool; contact your CSM to set that up.
- We’ll follow up with a short postmortem once the code-level fix is shipped.

Thanks for the quick responses — flag any anomalies here and we’ll investigate immediately.

— Logan
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
